description: Somos um grupo de 5 estudantes de graduação em engenharia e 1 um estudante de graduação em administração.
summary:
What We Developed:
E.S.G. (Extraterrestrial Survival Guide) Terminal is a dual-display EVA navigation and field-science system for Mount Sharp in Gale Crater, Mars. It pairs a minimalist Helmet Visor (HUD)—keeping the central view clear with peripheral telemetry (oxygen, slope, sample load, radiation, dust, and walkback alerts)—with a 16:9 Forearm LCD featuring a multi-layer map and science deck, operated hands-free via voice (EN/PT) or a single glove button.

How It Addresses the Challenge:
It unifies all five mandatory NASA/USGS datasets (Mars Trek, USGS Astrogeology, Curiosity's Proposed Path, Worldview, and Mars 2020 Raw Images) across a 940 m foot traverse to the Boxwork ridges. A 4-mode Autonomous Pathplanner fuses MOLA slopes (>15°), THEMIS sand traps (135 tiu), sample weight (+6.5 kg), radiation, and dust (Tau) to manage a Locked Point of No Return (1010 m) and a live Contingency Envelope.

Why It Is Important:
Steep scarps (16.8°) and loose sand (135 tiu) block wheeled rovers from reaching astrobiological targets like Mount Sharp's Boxwork ridges. E.S.G. Terminal bridges that final kilometer on foot, uniting orbital data and life-support safety.
details:
1. Target Martian Region & Scientific Data (Public Domain — NASA and USGS): E.S.G. Terminal targets the lower northwestern flank of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) in Gale Crater, Mars, guiding a 940 m foot traverse (+55 m ascent) from the pressurized EVA Rover staging point at WP-01 (Lower Murray Plain, -2440 m) to WP-04 (Boxwork Sulfate Ridges, -2385 m), with >=95% orbital-to-surface data confidence. It integrates five mandatory planetary datasets: • NASA Mars Trek: MOLA topographic contours (-2450 m to -2375 m), critical 16.8° scarp hazards, THEMIS thermal inertia (135 tiu loose sand traps to 345 tiu indurated bedrock), and CRISM spectral bands (2.30 µm clay/hematite and 1.94 µm polyhydrated sulfates). • USGS Astrogeology Interactive Maps: Stratigraphic contacts between the Murray Mudstone, Stimson Sandstone Unconformity, and Sulfate-Bearing Boxwork Unit. • Curiosity's Proposed Path Up Mount Sharp: Reference rover ascent trajectory and MSL-RAD surface radiation baseline (0.24 to 1.45 mSv/h). • NASA Worldview: Atmospheric dust optical depth (Tau 0.45 clear sky to 2.60 dust storm). • Mars 2020 Multimedia Raw Images: Integrated as an Analog Surface Texture Library for boot traction and core sampling preview at each waypoint.

2. Autonomous Pathplanning, Life-Support Physics & Field Science Integration: To reconcile astronaut safety with scientific collection, the mathematical engine calculates real-time Portable Life Support System (PLSS) O2 consumption by combining terrain slope, soil thermal inertia (tiu), base suit mass, cumulative geological sample weight (+2.5 kg to +6.5 kg), and station sampling duration (15 to 40 min). • Dual Point-of-No-Return (PNR) Architecture: The nominal Departure PNR (1010 m) is locked once the EVA walk begins, while a dynamic Contingency Walkback Envelope shrinks in real time if mid-traverse hazards erode O2 reserves. • 4-Mode Autonomous Pathplanner: Evaluates active hazards to switch automatically between Mode 1 (Nominal Ridge Ascent), Mode 2 (Low-Angle 6.4° Terrace Bypass when sample mass reduces biomechanical slope limits), Mode 3 (Northern Scarp Shelter Route at 8.5° grade providing -55% natural topographic shielding during Solar Energetic Particle events), and Mode 4 (Emergency Rover Abort along heading 232° SW).

3. Pressurized EVA Suit Ergonomics & Hands-Free Operation: Because astronauts cannot operate fine touchscreens while wearing rigid pressurized EVA gloves, E.S.G. Terminal divides situational awareness across two synchronized displays: • Astronaut Helmet Visor (HUD): Features a first-person Martian horizon that reacts dynamically to dust opacity (Tau) and solar radiation while keeping peripheral symbols unobtrusive. • 16:9 Forearm Wrist LCD: Toggles between a decluttered multi-layer tactical map (with semantic zoom from 50% to 200%, scale bar, compass rose, and satellite/vector basemap toggle) and a telemetry deck featuring a MOLA cross-section elevation profile. • Gloved & Voice Control: Operated 100% hands-free via bilingual voice recognition (EN-US and PT-BR with a >=95% confidence safety threshold) or via a single physical analog button on the forearm bezel.

4. Code Libraries, Visuals, Audio, AI Disclosure & Copyright Compliance: Built as a self-contained, 100% offline-capable web application in HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript using permissive open-source libraries: Tailwind CSS (MIT License), Font Awesome Free 6.5.1 (CC BY 4.0 / MIT), and Google Fonts Inter and JetBrains Mono (SIL OFL 1.1). Shaded-relief Digital Elevation Models, geological outcrop textures, and tactical audio alerts are procedurally generated via HTML5 Canvas, SVG, and the W3C Web Audio API, alongside hands-free voice control via the Web Speech API. Developed with Visual Studio Code, Chrome/Edge, and Google Gemini (used for code assistance and visual asset prototyping). All external planetary data is public domain (NASA/USGS).
